1.explanation:
• FileUploader/index.js: Entry point where FileUploader and its subcomponents (including the button) are wired up.
• FileUploader/FileUploaderButton.js: Contains the actual code that renders the <label> for the file upload button and where the stray role attribute is set.
• FileUploader/FileUploaderButton.story.js: Storybook example that reproduces the UI exactly as in the screenshot, useful for running DAP tests against it.
• Button/index.js: Provides the base styles and behaviors (e.g. bx--btn classes) that the FileUploaderButton wraps; helps understand how the element becomes button-like.
• FormLabel/FormLabel.js: Shows how labels are supposed to be rendered in Carbon and why adding a role here diverges from standard practice.
• README.md: Root documentation that shows how to integrate and run FileUploader in an app, including how to spin up Storybook, so you can reproduce and validate the DAP violation in your environment.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering the FileUploaderButton (“Add files”) UI, the component uses a native <label> element with a bare "role" attribute (no valid WAI-ARIA role value). Chrome’s DAP accessibility scan flags this as “Elements that use 'role' must reference a valid WAI-ARIA role.” In the screenshot you can see the DOM tree showing “<label role tabindex=\"0\" …>” wrapping the button styling, and the DAP panel reporting the violation. Removing the stray "role" attribute from the label fixes the error.
